headings.text: Driving Brand Engagement and Sales Through Influencer-Led Instagram Live Sessions and User-Generated Content Challenges

This integrated campaign combined influencer-led Instagram Live sessions with a user-generated content challenge to foster deeper connections with Chivita’s audience and increase product visibility and sales.

bodyText:
CHIVITA "12 Days of Christmas" Campaign
CHIVITA
ALL PROJECTS

Driving Brand Engagement and Sales Through Influencer-Led Instagram Live Sessions and User-Generated Content Challenges
This strategy created a dynamic, interactive experience that built a strong emotional connection with the audience, reinforcing Chivita’s position as a trusted and beloved brand during the holiday season.
Instagram Live Grotto Fiesta: Hosted by popular influencer Jay On Air, the Instagram Live sessions were designed to captivate the audience with interactive games, giveaways, and lively conversations. Guest appearances by influencers like Elozonam, Eki, Emeneks, Akin Faminu, and Noble Igwe further amplified the campaign’s reach and excitement.
​
​
This strategy not only attracted a significant number of viewers but also fostered a sense of community and brand loyalty. Early bird viewers were rewarded with product packs, and participants had the chance to win Christmas hampers, driving immediate interest in Chivita products and increasing product trial rates.
This integrated campaign combined influencer-led Instagram Live sessions with a user-generated content challenge to foster deeper connections with Chivita’s audience and increase product visibility and sales.
The “12 Days of Christmas” campaign for Chivita was a vibrant and festive initiative aimed at boosting brand engagement, awareness, and driving business impact during the holiday season.

bodyText:
Chivita 2.0 Campaign – “What’s Your Chivita?
CHIVITA
The “What’s Your Chivita?” campaign aimed to transform consumers into storytellers, using a network of influencers to anchor and amplify their experiences with Chivita products. The “What’s Your Chivita?” campaign successfully gave consumers a voice, using influencers to spark and anchor their stories.
Empowering Consumers Through Influencer-Led Content and User-Generated Stories. The “What’s Your Chivita?” campaign successfully gave consumers a voice, using influencers to spark and anchor their stories.
Influencer-Driven Narratives: The campaign strategically partnered with various influencers like Dianne Russet, Elozonam, and Teminikan, who integrated Chivita into their daily lives, creating authentic, relatable stories. Each influencer shared their personal experiences with Chivita, encouraging their followers to share their own using the #WhatsYourChivita hashtag, building a genuine connection between the brand and its audience.
User-Generated Content (UGC): By inviting consumers to share their Chivita moments, the campaign created a rich tapestry of user-generated content that resonated with a broad audience.
​
To maintain momentum and deepen engagement, we produced complementary content sand social media updates highlighting top user stories and influencer interactions. This contents kept the conversation alive and added layers to the campaign narrative, reinforcing Chivita’s brand message across various touchpoints.

bodyText:
Chivita and Hollandia Ramadan TVC
CHIVITA
ALL PROJECTS
The Future of Zenith — Zenith Bank
You Matter — Prudential Zenith Life Insurance
Live with Confidence — Sanlam Allianz
See for Yourself — Torrista
For the Ramadan season, Chivita and Hollandia partnered with our agency to create two impactful TV commercials aimed at resonating deeply with Nigerian and African consumers during this spiritually significant period.
These TVCs were designed to capture the essence of Ramadan, emphasizing community, togetherness, and the role of Chivita and Hollandia products in enhancing the season’s experiences.
The Chivita and Hollandia TVC focused on the theme of rejuvenation and refreshment from Iftar (evening meal) to Suhoor (pre-dawn meal) that breaks the fast. Both TVCs were tailored to resonate with the African audience, featuring culturally relevant storytelling, familiar traditional settings, and scenarios.

headings.text: CHIVITA STYLE N' SIPS YOUTUBE SERies

bodyText:
CHIVITA STYLE N' SIPS YOUTUBE SERies
CHIVITA
Designed to celebrate the joy of Chivita’s drinks through stylish, light-hearted content, the series aimed to increase brand visibility and engagement. By blending everyday themes, local relevance, and lively conversation, the series generated buzz and genuine audience connections, cementing Chivita’s position as a culturally attuned, fun-loving brand.
Influencer-Driven Amplification: To make sure we didn’t just reach audiences but also sparked conversations, we partnered with a diverse lineup of influencers like Elozonam, Akin Faminu, and Jay On Air. Each brought their own flair, voice, and loyal followers to the table. This wasn’t just about using their reach but making them part of the story, ensuring authentic content that viewers would love and share organically.
Multi-Platform Content Explosion: The series was strategically rolled out across Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube, with each platform playing a unique role. Paid promotion ensured we hit key audience segments at peak times, while organic growth allowed the content to flourish naturally among fans.
ALL PROJECTS
We Do Dreams — Prudential Zenith Life Insurance
See for Yourself — Torrista
Secure the Bag — i-invest
You Matter — Prudential Zenith Life Insurance
Authentic Storytelling Meets Social Media Flair: Chivita “Style N’ Sips” is not your average video series. We crafted episodes around trending topics and relatable themes—from “Boys Will Be Boys” to “Classic Elegance”—that would draw in diverse viewers. Each episode was a lively mix of style, humor, and real talk, designed to connect emotionally with viewers and position Chivita as a fun, refreshing, and accessible brand.

meta.description: Explore The Republic’s Cowbell Ramadan social campaign in Nigeria: preparation, recipes, sharing and recognition, with nearly 100 million recorded Meta views.
meta.og:title: Cowbell Ramadan Social Media Campaign | The Republic
meta.og:description: Explore The Republic’s Cowbell Ramadan social campaign in Nigeria: preparation, recipes, sharing and recognition, with nearly 100 million recorded Meta views.

bodyText:
YOUR FIRST TASTE
COWBELL RAMADAN
THE CAMPAIGN IN ACTION
Before the first taste, someone cared.
One human idea. A month of relevance. Nearly 100 million recorded Meta views.
Ramadan relevance is earned every day. Cowbell needed its campaign to stay useful across the month, beyond the launch film. We found the connecting thread in the care that happens before Sahoor and Iftar: someone prepares, someone shares, someone brings everyone to the table.
The Republic’s Nigeria digital and social execution turned “Your First Taste” into four recurring actions: prepare, make, share and recognise. Stock-up content, Sahoor ideas, regional meals and creator recipes made the brand useful. Sharing invitations, a 30-action calendar and thank-you prompts gave people ways to participate.
Each format did a different job. Together, they gave one human idea a consistent role throughout Ramadan.
The supplied Meta records show 99,999,862 views and 51,654 interactions across 44 Nigeria Facebook and Instagram posts, observed on 8 September 2026. Distribution was predominantly media-supported; these cumulative post views include repeat exposure.
The Republic: Nigeria digital and social execution within the wider regional campaign.
Social strategy · Content planning · Creator collaboration · Campaign amplification
Planning a seasonal campaign that needs to stay relevant beyond launch? Let’s talk.

meta.og:title: Onga Taste of Home: Digital Campaign Case Study | The Republic
meta.og:description: See how The Republic’s Onga Taste of Home platform connected creators, AMVCA Cultural Day and World Jollof Day, with 37.2M Instagram views on two launch films.

bodyText:
TASTE OF HOME
ONGA
Wherever the taste feels like yours, that’s home.
A digital brand platform connecting food, memory and participation—from the family kitchen to the World Jollof Day stage.
Onga’s improved Beef and Chicken cubes needed renewed consideration after three years of share decline. The opportunity was bigger than a product announcement: reconnect the brand with the food, people and memories that make somewhere feel like home.
Working with Promasidor Nigeria, The Republic built a digital platform people could participate in. We asked what home meant to them, brought their answers into the feed and made the thought tangible through creator cooking stories—including Stan Nze’s meal for Lolo.
Ramadan, family recipes and Kitchen Court kept the idea active in everyday life. Onga’s Food Creator Icon competition at AMVCA Cultural Day gave home cooking a public stage, with Chef Polan announced as its winner.
World Jollof Day carried the story into nominations, preparation and Nigeria–Ghana banter. Polan returned as Nigeria’s captain; Olusayo’s reporting brought the Ghana activities into the conversation. Creator recipes and customer comments brought the story back to the meals people make at home.
Two July launch-film records generated 37.2 million Instagram views and 1,470 follows. Nine specified Jollof and creator-recipe records separately recorded 7.98 million views. These are lifetime post metrics, including repeat exposure.
The Republic × Promasidor Nigeria | Digital strategy · Social content · Creator engagement · Campaign amplification
Need a brand platform people can join and keep coming back to? Let’s build it.

bodyText:
EMPOWERING TOMORROW
PRUDENTIAL ZENITH LIFE
Make tomorrow feel relevant today.
An integrated campaign connecting life’s ambitions with a more human conversation about protection and planning.
A business to grow. Children to put through school. A family to care for. Prudential Zenith Life needed to connect long-term protection with the ambitions people are working towards today.
Empowering Tomorrow made that future personal. The Republic brought creator conversations, future-self creative, outdoor and a digital planning journey together around one question: what kind of life are you building, and how will you protect it?
Oba and his dad opened the subject through humour. Olushola’s fireside discussion with Funmi Omo gave real questions space. The Tomorrow Pledge invited a personal response. “Boss in 2026. Boss in 2066.” carried the planning horizon into billboard creative, while radio extended the campaign into another everyday listening moment.
The supplied digital journey offered practical starting points: a Ready Test, planning tools and an invitation to speak with an advisor. Human stories opened the conversation; clearer next steps made it easier to continue.
The wider H1 2026 Google campaign report recorded 630K impressions and 1.66K website clicks. These are reported media results for the wider campaign, rather than outcomes attributed to an individual execution.
Strategy · Integrated communications · Creator content · Digital experience

headings.text: A STRATEGY CAMPAIGN TO MAKE INSURANCE FEEL HUMAN AGAIN
A Strategic Reset. Not just a Campaign

bodyText:
YOU MATTER CAMPAIGN
PRUDENTIAL ZENITH LIFE INSURANCE
A STRATEGY CAMPAIGN TO MAKE INSURANCE FEEL HUMAN AGAIN
Insurance is supposed to be personal, but in Nigeria, it rarely feels that way. People don't wake up thinking about cover. They think about school fees, rent, the future they haven't fully figured out. For Prudential Zenith Life, that was the challenge. How do we remind people that planning ahead isn’t just smart — it’s an act of love? How do we make a financial product feel like an emotional decision?
A Strategic Reset. Not just a Campaign
We knew this wasn’t about visibility — it was about relevance.So instead of selling a product, we sold a perspective: You Matter.Not as a tagline, but as a truth that cuts across media, culture, and behavior.

bodyText:
SHOW YOUR TRUE COLOURS
SPRUCE BY DULUX
THE CAMPAIGN IN ACTION
Preview your room in colour
Find your true colour
Picture Baddie Pink at home
Old Money Green meets Odogwu Red
From colour people noticed to colour they could consider choosing.
Digital amplification that connected Spruce’s personalities with conversation, room inspiration and the next step towards choice.
Liking a colour is easy. Choosing one for your space takes confidence. Spruce launched ten colours as ten recognisable personalities. Our digital task was to help that recognition work harder.
The Republic amplified the campaign through creators, social distribution and a clipper network. Akwaman and Jima, alongside Artmosfair and Stan Nze, made colour a conversation. Blog placements, including Tunde Ednut, gave the banter another route into the feed.
AI room inspiration and Pinterest content helped people picture the palette in Nigerian spaces. The case film follows that interest into the Spruce website’s room previews, personality quiz, pairings and product catalogue: practical ways to explore a choice.
The supplied report records 115 clipper posts against a week-one target of 25 — 4.6 times the target. Two individual clips recorded 222.1K and 126.9K views. Each is a separate post-view count.
The Republic: digital amplification, creator activity, social distribution and digital visualisation. Original concept and hero-film production credits remain with the originating teams.
Need to connect campaign attention with a more useful customer journey? Let’s talk.

bodyText:
OUR STORY
Creating Tomorrow
The Republic is an independent creative and marketing agency based in Lagos, Nigeria. We bring strategy, brand building, campaigns and digital execution together.
Our work starts with a clear business problem and a close understanding of the people a brand needs to reach.
Our manifesto
Clarity before volume
We solve for the right problem, then scale.
Systems over stunts
Big ideas become repeatable engines, not one-offs.
Outcomes over outputs
We measure what moves the business—brand, demand, and revenue.
OUR TEAM
A team that asks harder questions, makes the work simpler, and moves the numbers that matter. That’s what Creating Tomorrow looks like.
Where Vision Becomes Work
OLA OLOWU
Chairman

Torrista Visual Design – "See For Yourself" Brand Development Campaign
The Torrista brand-building campaign aimed to redefine travel experiences for Nigerians and Africans by making travel more accessible, affordable, and authentic.
Through the creative concept “See For Yourself,” we focused on showcasing Torrista’s core values—credibility, cultural richness, and seamless travel services—while inviting potential travelers to explore and engage firsthand.
Each visual element was designed to tell a story, drawing viewers in and encouraging them to “see for themselves” the unique travel experiences Torrista offers.

bodyText:
EVERYDAY HERO EVERYDAY TWISCO
TWISCO
The insight
Nigerian parents quietly celebrate the small, everyday hero moments where kids hack their way out of problems with limited resources. Yet no cocoa brand was speaking to that – or actively enabling it.
The challenge
Twisco had a strong micronutrient blend (Enerfort), but no clear emotional role. To mums, it was just one more brown drink. To kids, it wasn’t yet the exciting choice.
We needed to give Twisco a distinct, memorable role in Nigerian family life and make it a brand kids would actually ask for.

headings.text: The Zenith Bank 35th Anniversary campaign celebrated the brand’s legacy while projecting its future. Through immersive wall branding, we created a “tunnel of time” experience that showcased Zenith’s journey from inception to 35 years of excellence. Each wall featured portraits and milestones, allowing viewers to walk through the bank’s history in a powerful, visual way. meta.og:title: Zenith Bank Homecoming Campaign | The Republic
meta.og:description: Explore The Republic’s See Homecoming Differently strategy for Zenith Bank, connecting with Nigerians in the diaspora before travel and on their return home.

headings.text: They left to grow. They return to belong.

bodyText:
SEE HOMECOMING DIFFERENTLY
ZENITH BANK
They left to grow. They return to belong.
Every December, millions of Nigerians in the diaspora return home—not just for parties, but to reconnect, reset, and handle real life. The problem is that “coming home” often comes with friction: cards that don’t work, payment experiences that feel unfamiliar, and banking that isn’t ready the moment they land. We built a strategy that helps Zenith Bank own that first impression—before travel, at the airport, and across the first days back in Lagos.
